findings.title: installation_id is persisted before the OAuth state check
findings.body: OAuthLoginView copies installation_id from the query string into pipeline state before it verifies that state equals pipeline.signature. bind_state writes the session immediately (the happy path depends on that, because installation_id must survive the redirect to GitHub). A request that then fails the state check still returns the error page, but the overwritten installation_id remains. PipelineAdvancerView is CSRF-exempt and this endpoint is a top-level GET, so a cross-site navigation to /extensions/github/setup/?installation_id=<attacker>&state=invalid is enough to poison an in-progress install. The victim's later successful OAuth callback does not carry installation_id, and GitHubInstallation prefers the stored value. The victim's organization is then linked using the attacker's installation id.

findings.title: Installer identity is not checked on first install
findings.body: The new check that the OAuth login matches metadata['sender']['login'] runs only when an Integration row already exists and has no OrganizationIntegration. If Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) raises DoesNotExist, dispatch returns pipeline.next_step() and never reads github_authenticated_user. That is the normal first-install path: the installation webhook that records sender is asynchronous and often loses the race with the browser redirect, and build_integration only copies state['sender'] — it never receives or compares github_authenticated_user. Supplying an attacker installation_id (setup URL or the poisoned pipeline state) before that row exists links it to the victim's Sentry organization with no user check. The guarantee in the PR — fail on a mismatch between the OAuth user and the user who installed the GitHub App — is not enforced for new installations. The new test posts the webhook first, so it never covers this path.

findings.title: Re-link crashes when metadata has no sender
findings.body: On the re-link path the code indexes integration.metadata['sender']['login'] with no guard. build_integration only stores sender when pipeline state already has it, and this flow never writes github_authenticated_user into metadata. An ACTIVE Integration without a sender dict — older rows, rows created only by build_integration, or a webhook that stored sender under a different shape — raises KeyError or TypeError instead of the installation error page. The setup popup 500s and the re-link cannot finish.

findings.title: Non-active Integration rows can no longer be reinstalled
findings.body: Previously, an Integration that existed but had no OrganizationIntegration always continued to pipeline.next_step(), which re-fetches the GitHub installation and reactivates the record. The new lookup requires status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE and turns DoesNotExist into the generic authenticity error. ObjectStatus includes DISABLED, PENDING_DELETION, and HIDDEN, so a leftover non-active row with no org link — a normal uninstall leftover — now blocks reinstall. The message tells the user the request could not be verified and to restart, which cannot succeed until the row is deleted out of band.

findings.title: Token exchange omits redirect_uri sent on authorize
findings.body: The authorize redirect includes redirect_uri, but the code exchange posts only code, client_id, and client_secret. RFC 6749 section 4.1.3 requires the token request to repeat redirect_uri when it was included in the authorization request, and the values must be identical. GitHub's POST /login/oauth/access_token documents the same parameter and rejects mismatches (redirect_uri_mismatch or an invalid/expired code). The new tests stub that URL and return a token no matter the body, so they stay green if GitHub rejects the exchange and every real install stops on the generic error page. The authorize URL is also built by string interpolation rather than urlencode, so the redirect_uri GitHub records may not byte-match a later form-encoded value.

findings.title: OAuth network failures skip the installation error page
findings.body: safe_urlopen of the token endpoint and the following get_user_info call sit outside the try/except that maps a bad token body to the installation error page. A timeout, connection error, or ApiError from either call propagates as an unhandled 500 in the setup popup. This change is supposed to render github-integration-failed.html when GitHub cannot mint a token or the user cannot be identified; that page is only reached when body parsing fails or access_token/login is missing.

findings.title: installation-not-found test no longer hits the GitHub 404 path
findings.body: test_installation_not_found used to request setup_path with an installation_id and assert build_integration's 404 text "The GitHub installation could not be found." It now overwrites that response with a second request whose state is ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05, not the pipeline signature the other tests lock in (9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3), and asserts the generic "Invalid installation request." string. Unlike the updated happy-path tests it never calls init_path, so there is no session pipeline; PipelineAdvancerView redirects to / with "Invalid request.", which does not contain the new expected bytes. If a pipeline did exist, the wrong state is rejected in OAuthLoginView and the installations API is never called, so a regression in the 404 handling would not be caught.

findings.title: User-mismatch test posts a webhook with a stale signature
findings.body: test_github_user_mismatch changes INSTALLATION_EVENT_EXAMPLE (installation id and sender.login) but sends a static X-Hub-Signature of sha1=d184e6717f8bfbcc291ebc8c0756ee446c6c9486, the digest of the unmodified fixture. The webhook view HMACs the raw body, so this delivery is rejected and never creates an Integration whose sender is attacker; the assert resp.status_code == 204 fails when verification is enabled. The test then reuses state 9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3, captured for the default org, after login_as(user_2) and a new organization, and asserts the same "Invalid installation request." string that OAuthLoginView returns for a state mismatch. Neither a pass nor a fail shows that the sender comparison ran.
